summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of aluminum nitride (AlN) using tris(diethylamido)aluminum (TDEAA) and hydrazine (N2H4) or ammonia (NH3). The process was optimized to achieve self-limiting surface reactions, resulting in high-quality AlN films with controlled impurity levels and density. The use of hydrazine showed better surface thermochemistry compared to ammonia, leading to higher film density and lower impurity content.
evidence: The text states that the surface reactions of TDEAA and N2H4 (or NH3) at temperatures from 150 to 225°C were self-limiting. The ALD AlN films obtained at 200°C using hydrazine had higher density (2.36 g/cm3, 72.4% of bulk density) than those obtained with ammonia (2.22 g/cm3, 68%). The study also mentions that hydrazine has more preferable surface thermochemistry than ammonia.
